buyer_simulator.prompt: You write one text message from a homeowner to a home-service company that sent them an estimate. The facts this homeowner wants to get across in this message are given as a small JSON object. Put them in your own words, the way this particular person would text: 1-3 sentences, natural and specific to them, no emojis. Get every fact across and add nothing the facts do not say: no new requests or questions, no new numbers, no day, date or time that is not in the facts, no agreeing or refusing. Write figures and dates however this person would. What the acts mean: saw_it_only_now - they only now saw the estimate, it is fine, and they want a visit time; go_ahead - they are happy with it and want a visit time; cost_concern - the total is the problem (could_pay is what they could pay; give_a_figure false means name no figure); will_decide_later, needs_to_think, still_thinking - they have not decided and give no reason or date; wants_it_later, still_not_ready - they want the job, just not until about wait_weeks_about weeks from now; schedule_problem - the visit date offered does not suit them (give_reason false means say only that); needs_it_sooner - the visit date offered falls after the day it must be finished (done_by); household_must_review, household_still_discussing - someone else (who) has to see it too before they decide; household_view - they went through it with someone (discussed_with) and pass on that view. repeat true means they have said this before. Keep short private notes for your next message (under 40 words). Answer only with a JSON object: {"message": "...", "notes": "..."}
buyer_simulator.role: writes the buyer's words only; decisions are code (second_ask/tournament/env.py: react)

concession_heuristic.doc: naive gap-halving: concede half of the remaining gap to the floor (rounded to $5; straight to the floor under $20) at each objection or silence, every 4 days; quoted slot to a ready buyer. Not the heuristic of any paper

shop_rule.doc: discount to the owner's floor on the first objection or silence, then a reminder every 7 days; offers the quoted slot to a ready buyer

smart_rules.spec:
The strongest rule baseline we could write without a model. Frozen in the manifest (policies.smart_rules).

Inputs are only what the LLM policies see: the messages and their times, and how often the estimate was opened (the
coarse hint the other rule policies get is ignored). Same menu, same 3-day rhythm, prices only from the menu.
On the customer's latest unanswered message (lower-cased, ’ read as '), the first matching rule wins:
  1 an optional item named with "not needed / don't need / do without / skip / no need / without the" -> drop it
  2 a named $ amount below the current price (line-item prices excluded: those are references) -> of the drop and
    concede moves priced at or below the largest such amount, the one that keeps the most margin; none -> once,
    the lowest-priced drop or concede move; then answer
  3 sooner / too late / done by / by <day> / this week / tomorrow / urgent -> the earliest earlier slot, else
    offer_slot
  4 "N weeks" -> the check-in nearest to 7N days; "next month" -> 30; "later this month", "after the holidays",
    "not ready", "not yet" -> 14
  5 family words (wife, husband, partner, landlord, family, talk it over ...) -> ask_why once, then answer
  6 ready words (looks good, when can you, book, just saw, missed ...) -> offer_slot
  7 price words with no amount (expensive, more than, cheaper, budget ...) -> ask_why once, then the smallest
    concession (the highest-priced drop or concede move below the current price)
  8 think / get back / not sure / maybe -> ask_why once, then checkin_7
  9 anything else -> ask_why once, then answer
Silence (no reply since the shop's last message):
  no reply ever, estimate never opened, not resent yet -> resend on the other channel;
  the shop's last move was a check-in -> offer_slot; else ask_why once, then checkin_7.
Opt-out is the shared code layer (compliance.opt_out_status), as for every policy.

sanity_gates.booking_rate_per_policy: between 0.30 and 0.80 for the text-blind rule policies (shop_rule, concession_heuristic), dry run and full run
sanity_gates.invariants: bookings_above_walkaway == 0 and bookings_below_floor == 0 hold by construction (env.react, menu.validate): integrity checks, not evidence of realism

comparisons.secondary: every other policy vs smart_rules and vs shop_rule

scoring.compliance: violations = messages sent after a buyer asked to stop (per policy, n by opt-out style)
scoring.given_away_parts: given_to_full_payers = given_away of buyers whose walkaway >= the full list price; menu_gap = oracle - menu_oracle (booked buyers; unreachable with discrete menu prices); given_away = menu_gap + (menu_oracle - margin)
scoring.headline: $ per successful booking = model_usd / bookings; net = margin - model_usd
scoring.intervals: band: mean and [min, max] over repeats of the totals on the common subsample (the buyers every policy ran in every repeat), every policy on the same buyers; paired bootstrap (2000 draws, seed 7, 95 %) of the summed per-buyer difference
scoring.losing_cells: objection type x trade cells where routed earns less net per buyer than the best policy in the cell, on per-buyer means; with n per cell, a bootstrap interval of the mean per-buyer difference at 1 - 0.05/m (Bonferroni over the m cells with n >= 10); a clear loss needs n >= 10 and the interval below 0; the best policy is chosen in-sample, which biases toward a loss
scoring.lost: oracle (feasible buyers not booked); lost_price = the part from price-objection buyers
scoring.margin: booked price - cost of the booked package
scoring.menu_oracle: the same with real menu prices only (fresh offer on each package), at or below the walkaway
scoring.model_usd: sum of usage-based cost of the shop's Token Factory calls (buyer simulator excluded)
scoring.oracle: max over packages of min(list, walkaway) - cost, if >= the package floor; slot buyers need an open slot by their deadline; opt-out buyers are infeasible
scoring.totals: per buyer first: each buyer's mean over its repeats; then the sum over buyers (n = buyers). Only buyers finished in every policy and not excluded count (runner.final_rows)

home_cases.content: per archetype: id, objection type, trade and parameter ranges only
